source.title: Corrections to Introduction to Smooth Manifolds (Second Edition)

patch.content:
Example 1.31 (Spheres; corrected). Give $\mathbb{S}^n$ the graph charts from Example 1.4. On every nonempty overlap with distinct deleted-coordinate indices, for every choice of signs, the transition map deletes one coordinate and inserts the appropriately signed value of $\sqrt{1-|u|^2}$. Its domain keeps the radicand positive, so this map and its inverse are smooth. The positive and negative charts with the same deleted-coordinate index have disjoint domains. Hence these graph charts form the standard smooth atlas on $\mathbb{S}^n$.

_This is a faithful restatement of the official correction dated 2025-05-15._

patch.content:
Let $A\subseteq M$ and $F:A\to N$. If $N$ has empty boundary, Lee calls $F$ smooth on $A$ when, near each point of $A$, it agrees on $A$ with a smooth $N$-valued map defined on an open neighborhood in $M$. If $N$ has boundary, require instead a target chart around $F(p)$ that contains the nearby image; in that chart, the Euclidean-valued coordinate representation of $F$ must admit such a local smooth extension. This is Lee's local-extension convention for an arbitrary subset, not the same definition as merely having within-set derivatives.

_This is a faithful restatement of the official correction dated 2017-04-25._

patch.append_content: [Boundary convention from the official correction: when $p\in\partial M$, also allow curves parametrized on a one-sided interval with endpoint $0$, and take the derivative at $0$ from that side.]

[Officially corrected hypothesis and hint: at the boundary point $p$, assume $\ker dF_p\not\subseteq T_p\partial M$. In half-space coordinates, extend $F$ to an ambient Euclidean map. Choose a coordinate projection whose composite with the extension is a submersion, apply the ordinary rank theorem to that composite, and then use constant rank to show that the remaining coordinate functions are independent of the kernel variables along the half-space.]

We will see later that the smooth structure on $\partial M$ is unique. The correct forward reference is Problem 5-24, not Theorem 5.31.

entry.label: Problem 5-24
entry.content:
**English restatement.** Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold, and let $F : N \to M$ be smooth with image contained in $\partial M$. Prove that the corestricted map $N \to \partial M$ is smooth, and then deduce that $\partial M$ has a unique smooth structure for which it is an embedded submanifold of $M$.

**中文重述。** 设 $M$ 是带边界光滑流形，$N$ 是光滑流形，且光滑映射 $F : N \to M$ 的像包含在 $\partial M$ 中。证明把值域限制为 $\partial M$ 后所得的映射 $N \to \partial M$ 仍然光滑，并由此推出：使 $\partial M$ 成为 $M$ 的嵌入子流形的光滑结构是唯一的。

_This is a faithful bilingual restatement of the official erratum dated 2019-07-08._
